construction_markdown:
Let $p(T)=T^{30}+T+1$ and $K=\mathbb F_2[T]/(p)$, with $\alpha=T\bmod p$. Define the absolute trace $\operatorname{Tr}(z)=\sum_{r=0}^{29}z^{2^r}$ and $J=\{1,3,5,\ldots,65\}$. For $c\in\mathbb F_2$ and coefficients $a_j\in K$, set

$$w_{c,a}(x)=c+\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sum_{j\in J}a_jx^j\right),\qquad x\in K.$$

The code $C$ consists of all vectors $(w_{c,a}(x))_{x\in K}$. Order coordinates by writing $x=\sum_{i=0}^{29}u_i\alpha^i$ and sorting the integer $\sum_i u_i2^i$ increasingly. Thus every field, exponent, coefficient space, evaluation point, and coordinate order is deterministic. No puncturing, shortening, padding, or sampling is used.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For $K=\mathbb F_{2^m}$ and odd $D<2^m$, evaluation of $c+\operatorname{Tr}(\sum_{1\le j\le D,\ j\text{ odd}}a_jx^j)$ gives a binary linear code of dimension $1+m(D+1)/2$ and certified distance at least $2^{m-1}-(D-1)2^{m/2-1}$. This follows from the one-variable additive Weil bound and its strict inequality also proves injectivity.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: The generic Artin–Schreier conductor method stops exactly at 991 dimensions here. Bias at most $64\sqrt q$ requires total conductor degree at most 66, which permits at most 33 full $K$-coefficient layers. Degree 67 gives only $d\ge q/2-33\sqrt q=535,789,568$, falling short by 32,768. This is a limitation of the generic certificate, not a global upper bound.

distance_audit: For every nonzero polynomial part, its largest exponent is an odd integer $d\le65$, so the additive-character Weil bound applies without an Artin–Schreier exceptional case.
The case with zero polynomial part is separate: $c=1$ gives the all-one word of weight $2^{30}$.
The proof certifies a lower bound on $d_{\min}$; it does not claim that a word attaining the bound exists.
explicitness_audit: The field is concretely $\mathbb F_2[T]/(T^{30}+T+1)$; a Rabin irreducibility certificate is included in the proof.
The 33 exponents are exactly the odd integers from 1 through 65.
Every coefficient ranges over the full explicitly represented field; the constant $c$ ranges over $\mathbb F_2$.
The binary constant is deliberately outside the trace because $\operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbb F_2}(1)=0$ for extension degree 30.
Coordinates are all $2^{30}$ field elements in a specified polynomial-basis order.
No random choice, search-dependent object, padding, floor, puncturing, or hidden parameter occurs.
The current durable submissions, lemma book, roadmaps, and message board contained no files when audited.

obstructions: Generic degree 67 yields Walsh bound $66\sqrt q=2,162,688$, exceeding the allowed $64\sqrt q=2,097,152$. Its resulting distance certificate misses the target by 32,768.

More generally, for a full 2-reduced rational-function family on $\mathbb P^1$, conductor-only Hasse–Weil accounting permits at most 33 field-coefficient layers under this bias budget, hence at most 991 binary dimensions including the constant. This is only a method obstruction.

The full quadratic Reed–Muller layer cannot be added: it contains low-rank quadratic forms with bias far above $2^{-10}$. A six-layer Delsarte–Goethals subspace is valid but has only dimension 211 and is already contained in this 991-dimensional construction.
proof_markdown:
# Degree-65 trace-polynomial Reed–Muller subcode

## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with parameters

$$[2^{30},991,\ge 535{,}822{,}336]_2.$$

Its rate is $991/2^{30}=0.000000922940671443939208984375$.

## Field certificate

Set $p(T)=T^{30}+T+1$. To certify irreducibility, let $r_j=T^{2^j}\bmod p$, computed by $r_0=T$ and repeated squaring. Direct reduction gives

$$r_6=T^6+T^4,$$
$$r_{10}=T^9+T^8+T^7+T^4,$$
$$r_{15}=T^{27}+T^{26}+T^{24}+T^{21}+T^{20}+T^{17}+T^{15}+T^{14}+T^{12}+T^8,$$
$$r_{30}=T.$$

Writing $h_j=r_j+T$, the following Bézout congruences are directly checkable:

$$(T^4+T+1)p\equiv1\pmod {h_6},$$
$$(T^8+T^6+T^5+T^2+1)p\equiv1\pmod {h_{10}},$$
$$Ah_{15}\equiv1\pmod p,$$

where

$$A=T^{28}+T^{25}+T^{24}+T^{20}+T^{18}+T^{16}+T^{12}+T^9+T^2+T.$$

Thus $p$ is coprime to $T^{2^j}-T$ for $j=6,10,15$. Together with $r_{30}=T$, these are exactly Rabin's checks for the prime divisors $5,3,2$ of 30. Hence $p$ is irreducible and $K=\mathbb F_2[T]/(p)$ has exactly $2^{30}$ elements.

## Construction and linearity

Let $\alpha=T\bmod p$, let $\operatorname{Tr}(z)=\sum_{r=0}^{29}z^{2^r}$, and put $J=\{1,3,\ldots,65\}$. For $c\in\mathbb F_2$ and $a_j\in K$, define

$$P_a(X)=\sum_{j\in J}a_jX^j,
\qquad w_{c,a}=(c+\operatorname{Tr}(P_a(x)))_{x\in K}.$$

The coordinate order is the increasing binary-integer order of the coefficient vectors of $x$ in the basis $1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha^{29}$. Let $C$ be the set of all $w_{c,a}$. Trace, polynomial evaluation, and coefficient addition are $\mathbb F_2$-linear, so $C$ is binary linear. There is one coordinate for every $x\in K$, giving exact length $2^{30}$.

## Character-sum lemma

If $P\in K[X]$ has positive odd degree $d$, then

$$\left|\sum_{x\in K}(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(P(x))}\right|\le(d-1)\sqrt{|K|}.$$

For completeness, consider the smooth projective normalization of $y^2+y=P(x)$. Odd degree rules out $P=R^2+R$ over an algebraic closure: a finite pole of $R$ would survive with even order, while a polynomial $R$ would make $R^2+R$ have even degree. The affine curve is smooth because its derivative with respect to $y$ is 1. At infinity the degree-two Artin–Schreier extension is totally ramified. If $t=x^{-1}$ and $w(t)=2$, then $w(y)=-d$; the local uniformizer $t^{(d+1)/2}y$ shows that the different exponent is $d+1$. Riemann–Hurwitz therefore gives genus $g=(d-1)/2$, and there is one rational point above infinity.

For each $u\in K$, the equation $y^2+y=u$ has two solutions precisely when $\operatorname{Tr}(u)=0$, and none otherwise. Hence, with $S(P)=\sum_x(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(P(x))}$,

$$\#C(K)=|K|+1+S(P).$$

Hasse–Weil gives $|S(P)|\le2g\sqrt{|K|}=(d-1)\sqrt{|K|}$. This is also the standard one-variable additive Weil bound cited below.

## Exact dimension

The parameter space $\mathbb F_2\oplus K^{33}$ has binary dimension $1+33\cdot30=991$. It remains to prove injectivity. Suppose $w_{c,a}=0$. Evaluation at $x=0$ gives $c=0$. If some $a_j$ were nonzero, let $d$ be the largest such odd exponent. Then $1\le d\le65$, and the zero word would imply $S(P_a)=2^{30}$. The character-sum lemma instead gives

$$|S(P_a)|\le(d-1)2^{15}\le64\cdot2^{15}=2^{21}<2^{30},$$

a contradiction. Thus every $a_j=0$, proving injectivity and $\dim C=991$.

## Minimum distance

For any parameter tuple,

$$\operatorname{wt}(w_{c,a})=
\frac{2^{30}-(-1)^cS(P_a)}2.$$

If $P_a\ne0$, the lemma yields

$$\operatorname{wt}(w_{c,a})\ge
\frac{2^{30}-2^{21}}2
=2^{29}-2^{20}
=535{,}822{,}336.$$

If $P_a=0$, the only nonzero word has $c=1$ and weight $2^{30}$. Hence every nonzero word meets the target and

$$d_{\min}(C)\ge535{,}822{,}336
=\left(\frac12-2^{-10}\right)2^{30}.$$

## Reed–Muller relation

The $j=1$ coefficient and $c$ give every affine Boolean function, so $\operatorname{RM}(1,30)\subset C$. If $j=\sum_r2^r$, the map $x\mapsto x^j$ is a product of $\operatorname{wt}_2(j)$ Frobenius-linear maps. Therefore $\operatorname{Tr}(a_jx^j)$ has algebraic degree at most $\operatorname{wt}_2(j)$. The largest binary weight among $1\le j\le65$ is six, attained at $j=63$. Consequently

$$\operatorname{RM}(1,30)\subset C\subseteq\operatorname{RM}(6,30),$$

so this is a genuine Reed–Muller extension of the verified baseline.

## References

The character-sum theorem appears as Theorem 3.2 in E. Kowalski, [The Riemann Hypothesis for sums in one variable over finite fields](https://people.math.ethz.ch/~kowalski/exponential-sums-elementary.pdf). The irreducibility criterion is from M. O. Rabin, [Probabilistic Algorithms in Finite Fields](https://doi.org/10.1137/0209024), SIAM Journal on Computing 9 (1980), 273–280.
